result.handoff:
# Plan: Accept the short INIT-x.y code wherever a Work id is passed (INIT-2.4)

## Finding (P1)
Caller-supplied Work ids enter through exactly two services:
- WorkService: show (186), inspect (217), refresh (222), checkout (227), start (283), resume (350), trace (386), complete (474) — backing work show/checkout, change show/refresh, and every stage command.
- PublicationService: automatic/syncExclusive with input.workId — backing sync --work and the post-stage publication in cli/command.ts publish().

Validation is scattered (manifest-store.ts:102, publication.ts:133, sync.ts:14, worktree.ts:99/137), but every path funnels through GitManifestStore, and GitManifestStore.list() (manifest-store.ts:132) already enumerates every known Work id from manifest refs, archive refs, and the base. Stored-state parsers (work-manifest.ts, initiative-document.ts) validate canonical ids of persisted data and stay exactly as they are.

## Product files Build touches
1. src/core/identifiers.ts — add `WORK_CODE = /^INIT-\d+\.\d+$/` beside WORK_ID.
2. src/adapters/manifest-store.ts — add `resolve(idOrCode: string): Promise<string>`: a full WORK_ID returns as-is (existence stays read's job); a WORK_CODE enumerates ids the way list() does, matches those starting with `<code>-`, returns the single match (unique by construction), and throws INVALID_WORK_ID naming the input when none matches; anything else throws INVALID_WORK_ID as today.
3. src/application/work-service.ts — each of the eight entry methods resolves `workId = await this.store.resolve(workId)` first; the rest of each method is unchanged and sees the canonical id.
4. src/application/publication.ts — automatic and syncExclusive resolve input.workId through the store instead of rejecting non-WORK_ID input (the resolution replaces the WORK_ID test at line 133); the scope passed to remote.sync therefore always carries the canonical id, so matchesScope keeps working.
5. src/cli/commands/sync.ts — the --work flag validation accepts WORK_ID or WORK_CODE.
6. Tests: src/test/work-service.test.ts, src/test/publication.test.ts, src/test/cli-registry.test.ts.

Deliberately untouched: worktree.ts and the manifest parsers (they only ever see canonical ids after resolution), and the resolve path adds no git call for full ids (the common case).

## Tests (P3)
1. work-service.test.ts — plan start with the short code: works.start("plan", "INIT-0.1", ...) starts the run exactly as the full id (acceptance 1); show resolves the short code to the same Work view (acceptance 2 at the service that backs every command); an unknown code ("INIT-0.9") rejects with INVALID_WORK_ID naming the input (acceptance 3).
2. publication.test.ts — a scoped publication with the short code publishes only that Work, proving scope filtering still receives the canonical id (acceptance 2).
3. cli-registry.test.ts — sync.run accepts a short code for --work and still rejects garbage with INVALID_WORK_ID (acceptances 2–3).
4. The full existing suite is the regression proof that slugged ids keep working unchanged (acceptance 3).

## Acceptance coverage
1. plan start INIT-x.y starts the run like the full id — resolution at WorkService.start + test 1.
2. Short code works in every work-id command — all commands funnel through WorkService/PublicationService + tests 1–3.
3. Unknown code fails with INVALID_WORK_ID; full ids unchanged — resolver error + test 1's unknown case + existing suite.

## Verification for Build
npm run verify (typecheck, unit tests, smoke, --help).

## Non-goals
No ambiguity handling (the number pair is unique by construction). No change to what gets stored, printed, or projected: canonical slugged ids remain the only persisted form; resolution is an input convenience only. No short forms for Initiative ids.

traces.message: Caller-supplied Work ids enter through WorkService's eight methods (show, inspect, refresh, checkout, start, resume, trace, complete) and PublicationService (automatic/reconcile/syncExclusive with input.workId, used for sync --work and post-stage publication). Validation is scattered: manifest-store read (line 102), publication.ts:133, sync.ts:14, worktree.ts — but every path funnels through GitManifestStore, whose list() already enumerates all known ids from manifest/archive refs and the base. Stored-state parsers (work-manifest.ts, initiative-document.ts) keep requiring full ids and are untouched.

One resolution point: GitManifestStore.resolve(idOrCode). A full WORK_ID returns as-is; a WORK_CODE (/^INIT-\d+\.\d+$/, added to identifiers.ts) resolves against the same enumeration list() uses, matching ids that start with "<code>-"; exactly one is possible by construction, zero throws INVALID_WORK_ID naming what was passed. WorkService resolves at the top of each of its eight methods and PublicationService at automatic/syncExclusive, so everything downstream — refs, branches, scope filters — always sees the canonical slugged id. The sync CLI flag validation accepts both forms.

Tests: work-service.test.ts gains short-code coverage — show resolves, plan start with a short code starts the run (acceptance 1), and an unknown code fails INVALID_WORK_ID (acceptance 3); publication.test.ts gains a scoped sync by short code that publishes only that Work; cli-registry.test.ts asserts sync --work accepts a short code and still rejects garbage. Existing full-id tests are the regression proof that full ids keep working (acceptance 3).

Testing covers the resolution paths optimally.

result.handoff:
# Build: INIT-2.4

## Changed files (product)
- src/adapters/manifest-store.ts — new `resolve(idOrCode: string): Promise<string>`: a full WORK_ID returns as-is (no extra git call); a WORK_CODE enumerates the same refs `list()` walks and returns the unique match (throws INVALID_WORK_ID for no match, STATE_CORRUPT for non-unique).
- src/application/work-service.ts — each of the eight entry methods (show, inspect, refresh, checkout, start, resume, trace, complete) calls `workId = await this.store.resolve(workId)` as the first line, so downstream sees the canonical id.
- src/application/publication.ts — `automatic` and `syncExclusive` resolve `input.workId` through the store instead of testing WORK_ID format; the scope passed to `remote.sync`, the issue-resolution scope, and the per-Work entry lookup all use the canonical id; WORK_ID import removed.
- src/cli/commands/sync.ts — the --work flag validation accepts WORK_ID or WORK_CODE.
- src/test/work-service.test.ts — two new tests: short code resolves to the same view/run as the full id, and an unknown short code fails with INVALID_WORK_ID naming the input.
- src/test/publication.test.ts — new test: a scoped publication by short code publishes only that Work.
- src/test/cli-registry.test.ts — new test: sync --work accepts a short code and forwards it to the service.

## Validation
- `npm run verify` green: typecheck, 257/257 unit tests (4 new), smoke, --help.

## Commits
- 91b0f38 INIT-2.4-accept-the-short-init-x-y-code-wherever-a-work-i: Accept the short INIT-x.y code wherever a Work id is passed (product)
- 53b9aac codepatrol(INIT-2.4-accept-the-short-init-x-y-code-wherever-a-work-i): manifest projection (state update for the active Build run)

## Candidate
- The product commit `91b0f38` carries every code and test change. The branch head `53b9aac` is the manifest projection that the Build run wrote on its way to completion. Both are clean and reproducible from `e6a6e71`.

## Acceptance
1. plan start with a short code resolves the unique Work and starts the run like the full id — WorkService.start resolves at entry + the new work-service test.
2. The short code resolves in every work-id command — every command funnels through WorkService or PublicationService, both of which now resolve; new tests in work-service, publication, and cli-registry pin the behavior at the three call sites that back stage commands, sync --work, and the post-stage publication.
3. An unknown short code fails with INVALID_WORK_ID naming the input, and the full slugged id keeps working — the resolver throws INVALID_WORK_ID with the input in the message (new work-service test); the full slugged id is the common path of `resolve` (returns as-is), and the full existing suite passes unchanged.

## Notes
- A bug surfaced and was fixed during Build: the new `syncExclusive` had to use the resolved `workId` (not the raw `input.workId`) when feeding `resolveIssues` and when looking up the scoped entry, or the scoped publication would have produced zero Issues. The fix is one-line and the regression test (scoped publication by short code) pins it.
